answer: A copper escrow can make each paid task carry its own collateral: the agent locks a deposit released only when a small jury of randomly chosen peers attests the work, with the vine of reputation linking past verdicts to future trust. An identity caught near the nadir of its score loses its deposit and its standing, so one operator running many fake agents must fund a separate deposit for every identity and risks losing all of them at once. Honest agents pay nothing beyond the refundable deposit, while a sybil farm's attack cost scales with the number of identities it must keep capitalized.
